reading.title: Saving a dying town
reading.text: Ten years ago, Hollowfield was on a downward trajectory: the mine had closed and young people were leaving. When the council proposed a giant shopping centre, residents rejected the plan, objecting that it would destroy the historic centre. Instead, a local group launched a project to turn empty buildings into studios for artists. The government injected two million pounds into the scheme, subject to strict conditions on how the money was spent. Opinions about the results are subjective, but visitor numbers have tripled and the population is growing again.
